keyframe_review.note: 13,421 km2: a band that runs from the Dniester near 47.9N 24.4E north-east to 49.6N 27.1E. The page names Terebovlia as capital; the gazetteer puts that town 27 km from the nearest cell of the shape (Ternopil 50 km, Halych 60 km), so the principality's heartland is not drawn. The page gives no extent and no area; the correction adds a 50 km disc round the capital as a reading, not a boundary.

keyframe_review.note: 57,392 km2: the 1085 band grows by 172 cells (about 43,000 km2) south and east over Podolia, the Dniester and the Prut (Kamianets-Podilskyi, Chernivtsi, Vinnytsia, Botosani and Suceava lie inside). No page opened dates or describes that growth; the page gives no area. As for 1085, the capital's own land is missing and is added; the Podolian and Moldavian reach is unverified: page budget (2 pages).

ledger.note: 1084: Terebovlia is established as an appanage for Vasylko Rostyslavych. The page: 'established as an appanage around the year 1084 and given to Vasylko Rostyslavych'; the infobox 'Established: 1084'. The Vasylko page says 'He was the first Prince of Terebovl' from 1092'. The Council of Liubech page has the Rostislavichi Volodar and Vasilko receiving Peremyshl, Terebovl and Cherven jointly on 19 October 1097.

region.text: the Podolian and Dniester-Prut land Cliopatria adds in 1094

ledger.note: 1094: Cliopatria widens the principality south and east over Podolia and the Dniester-Prut lands (+43,000 km2). The pages opened say nothing of this land, of 1094 or of any conquest; the date and the land are Cliopatria's, kept as a bridge.

1124: Vasylko Rostyslavych dies and his son Rostyslav-Hryhoriy succeeds (the page's list: Vasylko 1084-1124, Rostyslav-Hryhoriy 1124-1141). The page: 'After Vasylko Rostyslavych died in 1124, Halych principality seceded,' after which the territory was absorbed. The Vasylko page gives his life as 'c. 1066 - 1124'. A change of prince on the same land; the page does not say what 'seceded' took from Terebovlia.

wars.name: War after the blinding of Vasylko Rostyslavych
wars.outcome: David Igorevich and Sviatopolk II captured and blinded Vasylko in November 1097, which broke the Liubech agreements and brought war; the page gives no result for Terebovlia.
wars.note: The Vasylko page: 'the agreements reached at an earlier meeting of the princes at the Council of Liubech were broken and war ensued.' It gives no year for the war's course or end, so 'to' is the blinding year; no border is shown to move.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line on the pages opened; the frontiers with Hungary, Peremyshl and the steppe are approximate throughout.

notes: Pages opened: Principality of Terebovlia, Vasylko Rostyslavych (budget 1-2) and, for the Liubech grant, the Council of Liubech page also read for the Ryazan dossier. End 1141 follows the page; Cliopatria's 1146 and its Halych row from 1147 leave 1142-1146 to the Halych dossier's author. The Cliopatria shape is a band 27 km from the capital: the correction adds a 50 km disc (a lon/lat radius because the gazetteer has no 'Terebovlia'; gazetteer name needed: Terebovlia, place, 49.30N 25.72E, Ternopil oblast). Pages disagree on the first prince's date (Terebovlia page 1084, Vasylko page 1092). The 1094 growth over Podolia and the Prut is not on any page opened. The Council of Liubech page (as read) gives Peremyshl, Terebovl and Cherven jointly to Volodar and Vasilko, which the principality-of-peremyshl dossier should reflect; 1210-1211 appanage of Iziaslav Volodymyrovych is after the end and not drawn.
